rules.statement: Pick the handler for a polymorphic payload deterministically from an explicit type discriminator; do not try one parser or algorithm after another and catch the exceptions to guess the type.
rules.why: Guessing with exceptions as control flow is nondeterministic and fragile. A required discriminator picks the right handler directly and leaves the catalog as the extension point.
rules.check: Look for try/catch chains that attempt one format or algorithm (e.g. RSA, then ECC), swallow the failure and fall through to the next one to work out what kind of input arrived.

rules.statement: When per-type behavior is modeled as a registered descriptor or strategy catalog, put each new per-type operation (generate, import, serialize/deserialize, export) on that descriptor and resolve it by key; do not add a hardcoded switch on the type, or a second parallel strategy registry, in consuming services.
rules.why: Spreading one type's behavior across several seams means a new type has to touch unrelated code, and it invites drift such as a type that can be exported or persisted but not deserialized.
rules.check: Look for new `switch`/if-chains on a type discriminator in services that could resolve a descriptor instead, or a new per-type converter/strategy interface that duplicates an existing descriptor catalog.

rules.statement: A public abstract base class meant for extension must not require constructor dependencies that only some derived families use; inject such a dependency on the intermediate base that actually uses it.
rules.why: Putting a dependency on every extender couples custom implementations to a low-level primitive they don't need, and blurs which type is the real extension seam.
rules.check: Look for constructor parameters on a public extensibility base class that the base itself never uses and only some subclasses consume.

rules.statement: Move state and behavior that sibling concrete classes declare identically into their shared base class, so each concrete holds only what actually differs.
rules.why: Duplicated metadata and certificate handling across sibling classes invites drift, where the same state ends up handled differently in each concrete.
rules.check: Look for sibling classes that re-declare the same properties, fields or helper methods with identical implementations instead of inheriting them from a common base.

rules.statement: Do not keep a public constant or discriminator value that no registered handler can process or round-trip; remove it instead of keeping it for compatibility, at least while the package is pre-release.
rules.why: A public value that persists but can't be deserialized is a latent trap, and a pre-release posture favors removing a broken shape over preserving it.
rules.check: Look for public constants or enum values used as type discriminators that have no matching catalog entry or handler, or that exist only for back-compat while being unusable.
